quickref.name: Aztec Attack (originally "Facing Temples")
quickref.era: Added BBR v1.3.1, June 28, 2012, as "Facing Temples" [Game text via wiki]. Renamed Aztec Attack at the 2013 BBG relaunch: the wiki says "up until version 2.0", the page was moved 2013-06-04 and SkyVu used the aztec-attack URL slug by Aug 2013. No map-specific rework is documented; BBG 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021) brought game-wide "New Map Lighting". The wiki says servers shut down Mar 12, 2024.
quickref.in_2026: Shown in the official Steam trailer at 12.0–16.0 s and 43.0–45.5 s [Observed]. "Aztec Attack" is track 13 (1:20) of the official 2026 OST [Canon]. A fan video of playtest #3 (Aug 21, 2026) has the chapter "Aztec Attack FFA". The Steam store text does not name it, so launch inclusion is a strong inference.
quickref.setting: A night-time Mesoamerican-style temple arena on a peanut-shaped plateau island ringed by a lava sea. Two big stepped sandstone pyramids face each other; team bases are inside the temples [Fan-wiki]. A central lava pool holds a faceted obsidian rock and a line of stepping stones, with a ruined colonnaded pavilion on each side.
quickref.palette_and_lighting: Night: deep indigo zenith #05032B with stars, then plum #450930, crimson #830E2D and a raspberry horizon #9D1238 over black-maroon hills #3B0605. Sand is burnt orange #D85C2B (2026; #78421F in 2012). Sandstone #A85732 to #B26137. Lava sea #FF9A11; pool core #FEA604 to #FBCF02. Obsidian #220301. Cyan pads #46C7D4; red-team panels #CD3823. Warm light thrown up from the lava, soft shadows, cool accents only from pads and gems. No weather or particles seen in stills.
quickref.landmarks: (1) Twin stepped temples facing each other. (2) A grand front staircase to a dark doorway framed by teal, coral and violet gem-mosaic panels and scroll reliefs. (3) The central lava pool with an obsidian rock and stepping stones. (4) The lava sea around the island. (5) Two ruined colonnaded pavilions beside the pool. (6) Carved mask-face stone cubes on cracked sand. Also: summit shrines with pyramidal caps, and a colonnade of square pillars around each temple base.
quickref.hazards_and_easter_eggs: Lava kills, and the death counts as a suicide [Fan-wiki]. Many jump pads: the wiki says 12, I counted 14 markers. Some go up the back of each temple to a summit sniper perch, some sit at the pool corners and two are on the central rock. The Bearscream Sandwich is on the central rock [Fan-wiki]. The wiki claims Over Clocked Oliver and Astoria symbols at the temple spawns [Fan-wiki, Unverified; not seen in any image]. The name may nod to Unreal Tournament's Facing Worlds [Fan-wiki speculation]. Flames seen in one fan thumbnail are a weapon glitch, not set dressing.

corrections.current_text: - [OFFICIAL-FRAME] The BBG in-game 3D look (Steam screenshots and the Steam trailer; the lava caverns are from the trailer) uses chunky, simple low-poly models and highly saturated colour. Interiors are glossy white and red sci-fi, there are lava/orange caverns and rocky caves, and effects are bright magenta, cyan and yellow.
corrections.correction: Replace "lava/orange caverns" and "the lava caverns are from the trailer". The trailer's lava is the open-air Aztec Attack map: a plateau island in a lava sea under a starry crimson-to-indigo night sky (12.0–16.0 s and 43.0–45.5 s) [Observed]. The enclosed red-orange space at about 38.5–41.0 s is a fleshy interior with veined walls and rib-like columns, probably Marecraft [Inference], not a lava cavern.

corrections.current_text: - **Aztec Attack**: temple carvings of O.C.O. and Astoria. The wiki speculates this "may show that Oliver has a crush on Astoria", which is fan speculation. [Fandom](https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Aztec_Attack)
corrections.correction: Use the wiki's exact, hedged wording. The Aztec page: "One temple has a symbol representing Over Clocked Oliver, while the other has a symbol representing Astoria." The OCO page: "there seems to be a carving of Over Clocked Oliver, along with Astoria. Both are located at each team's spawn points." Note that no image checked from 2012 to 2026 shows these symbols; the visible carvings are generic Mesoamerican masks, scrolls and gem mosaics. Add the basics: two temples on a lava-ringed island; added in BBR v1.3.1 (June 28, 2012) as Facing Temples.
